title: Cairn midwatch pocket manual
content:
Purpose: quick midwatch companion for when I'm covering the 00:00–06:00 window. Not a formal runbook — condensed tips, short commands, and temporary mitigations I actually used in the last two incidents. Keep this on the laptop top of mind; pass notes to the next person in the morning in #sre-shift-handoff.

Shift summary (what I saw at start):
- Cluster: prod-us-west-2 healthy; 3/4 autoscaler controllers green, one flapping ALB -> transient 503s at 23:40 local.
- Queue depth: inference-requests SQS ~ 120 (normal < 50). Spike started ~22:50, steadying after 00:15.
- Observability: ingestion-service latency p95 ~ 320ms (target < 200ms) on a subset of pods.

Active issues and status:
1) Inference queue backlog (severity: medium) — mitigation in progress.
   - Symptom: sudden increase in user-side async requests; many retries.
   - Action taken: enabled temporary rate-limiter rule at edge (api-gateway) to throttle non-critical clients.
   - Temporary mitigation: added a short-lived routing policy to spill to dedicated-fallback model group for lower-cost, lower-latency responses.
   - Current: backlog reduced to ~40, still monitoring. Ticket ENG-2187 created.

2) Intermittent 503s from ALB (severity: low) — intermittent health-check failures.
   - Symptom: ALB logs show 5xx from ingress-controller at 23:38–23:45.
   - Action taken: cycled ingress-controller pods one at a time; increased health-check timeout from 3s -> 6s while investigating.
   - Follow-up: add longer backoff in deployer for heavy-rollout windows.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes on alert):
- Run: kubectl get pods -n platform -o wide | grep -E 'ingress|ingestion|inference'
- Check: grafana -> "prod-overview" -> token-level latency, queue depth, pod OOM graphs.
- If p95 > 300ms: inspect the top 3 pods by latency and dump stack: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -p -- cat /proc/1/stack (or attach gdb if native crash).
- If queue grows > x2 baseline: consider short-term rate-limit at gateway + enable fallback model group.

Temporary mitigations I use (short-lived, document and revert):
- Edge throttle (api-gateway): add header-based rule to reduce concurrency from 100 -> 20 for client-type:experimental. Revert after 2h or when backlog < 30.
- Model spill: route requests tagged 'latency-sensitive=false' to model:a21-fallback-quantized. Add audit entry in #sre-night-ops with the reason and ticket number.
- Pod bounce for ingress: drain and recreate one pod at a time with a 30s wait; do not scale-to-zero during incidents.

Commands I ran tonight (copy to morning notes if needed):
- kubectl -n inference get hpa
- aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url <inference-queue> --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessages
- oc logs deploy/ingress-controller -n platform --since=2h | grep 503 | tail -n 200
- curl -v -H 'x-client: smoke' https://api.redwood.ai/health (use from jump host)

Escalation contacts (order):
- On-call infra (pager): Marcus Li (pager: primary). Slack: @marcusli.
- Serving runtime lead: Jordan Kim — if model spill / quantization mismatch suspected.
- Product on-call: Priya Desai for customer-impacting SLA questions.
- Pager policy: 30m unresolved active degradation -> escalate.

Short playbook snippets (for common alerts):
- High inference latency (p95 > 400ms): check model hot-cache hits, KV cache rate, and whether pods are getting preempted. If cache hit-rate < 60% -> enable prefix cache warmup for high-traffic keys (one-off script: ops/cache-warmup.py --model <model-id> --keys-file /tmp/hot-keys).
- Pod OOMKill cycle: identify container memory requests vs limits. If observed OOMKilled > 3 times in 10m, increase limit by +20% on the failing pool and open follow-up for memory profiling.
- ALB 5xx spike: examine target group health, increase healthy threshold to 3 -> 4 (temporary) and investigate NLB target metrics.

Known gaps / TODOs (non-blocking but important):
- Add a short run to the deployer to set longer health-check window during rolling updates (PR stub: ops/deployer#601).
- Build a small dashboard for queue vs model throughput per region (requested in ENG-2198).
- Automate the edge-throttle rule via api-config so we can toggle via the Console instead of manual toggle.

Notes to morning shift (things I'd like reviewed):
- Verify that model spill didn't cause quality regressions for the top 5 customers. See sampling: /samples/spill-a21-20241109.tgz in S3.
- Confirm ALB errors did not correlate with deployer rollouts (I saw a rollout at 23:35 but it seems unrelated; still check commit hash).
- Follow up with infra on increased EBS latency observed on host ip-10-0-71-12 between 00:30–01:10.

Scratch commands and snippets I keep in my pocket: (copy/paste ready)
- Short throttle add: curl -X POST https://edge-config.internal/v1/rate-limits -d '{"rule":"client:experimental","limit":20,"ttl":"2h"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
- Roll single ingress pod: kubectl -n platform delete pod $(kubectl -n platform get pod -l app=ingress-controller -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') --grace-period=30
- Snapshot SQS: aws sqs receive-message --queue-url <url> --max-number-of-messages 10 --visibility-timeout 300

Handoff checklist (what I'm leaving for you):
- Backlog snapshot: inference queue = 40 (was 120) 
- Edge throttle active until: 2024-11-10T02:10:00Z (please remove if traffic normal).
- Model spill active -> model:a21-fallback-quantized (revert after morning validation).
- Incident ticket: ENG-2187 (details + links in ticket).
- Key logs saved to: s3://redwood-ops/nightlogs/2024-11-09/cairn-midwatch.zip (contains grafana screenshots and pod logs).

Two questions for follow-up:
1) Is prefix caching for inference safe for the new evaluation families we onboarded last week? If not, we need a canary to test cache correctness.
2) Why did we see EBS latency on 10-0-71-12 only in us-west-2? Was there a noisy neighbor or snapshot job?

Personal reminders (notes to self):
- Next time: when enabling model spill, toggle a small sampling flag so we can collect side-by-side quality metrics automatically.
- Add a short play to the SRE runbook that documents safe throttle limits per client tier.

If you take over from me: drop a quick note in #sre-shift-handoff with these items and ping Marcus if anything persists beyond 30m. I'll check in remote in the morning (UTC-8) if anything bubbled.

— Aisha
